title: Transcript to Action Plan
tagline: Turn a client meeting transcript into the follow-up email you post into Neoserra — Next Steps, Notes, Accomplishments, Links — plus a menu of extras and the Nexus counseling narrative.
summary: Paste or attach the transcript of a client meeting and you get back the professional follow-up email, written in your voice to the client, sorted into the four sections Neoserra expects. It is the record of the meeting, not a chronological dump.

After the draft, it offers a short lettered menu of follow-ups built from this meeting: a capital-readiness scorecard, a recommended training plan, the Maryland good-standing check, a funding search when capital came up, and a Nexus/Neoserra mapping option that gives you the exact dropdowns to enter and the third-person session narrative that survives a Form 641 review.
never: Never uses emojis or casual tone — the email becomes part of the client's official record.
Never mixes inferred or partial milestones with confirmed ones; anything uncertain goes in a separate table for you to verify.
Never sends anything. You copy the email into Neoserra and your mail client yourself.
have_ready: The transcript — pasted, attached, or a Google Meet / Zoom export. A detailed description of the meeting works if that's all you have.
Optional: the client's Neoserra file, if you want milestones mined from it.
Optional: the current Neoserra Training Events export, if you'll ask for the training plan.

connects.does: When you pick the funding-search option and the connector is available, the search runs live instead of from memory
Gives you the entity-search link to click through for the good-standing check

setup.first_say: Here's the transcript from my meeting with [client] — draft the follow-up email.
asks: Nothing, usually. It drafts from the transcript and asks only if something blocks the draft (a client name, a missing link).

say: Draft the SBDC next-steps email from this transcript.
Flag the Neoserra milestones from this conversation.
Map this meeting to the Nexus/Neoserra dropdowns.
returns: The email — Subject SBDC Next Steps - [Client ID] - [Company], then Next Steps, Notes, Things We Have Accomplished Since Our Last Meeting, Relevant Links.
Milestones it spotted (certifications like 8(a)/MBE/WBE/DBE, sales or expansion, legislative letters, AI adoption, surveys), with anything uncertain in a separate verification table.

A lettered follow-up menu — always the scorecard, training plan, and good-standing check; funding search and hand-offs to other toolkit skills when the meeting calls for them; two or three ideas invented for this meeting; one "high value, minimum effort" pick; and the Nexus/Neoserra mapping.
then: Pick a letter to get that deliverable.
The Neoserra option returns both the dropdown selections and the full narrative — paste the narrative as the counseling note.
Post the email into Neoserra, then send it to the client from your own mail.
tips: Say the client ID and company up front and the subject line comes out right the first time.
If the client mentioned funding, the funding-search option is the one to pick — it's live when the Compass connector is on.

faq.q: Is this the same as the ChatGPT "Transcript to Action Plan 2.0" assistant?
faq.a: Same method, same output shape. This is the Claude version inside the toolkit plugin.

faq.q: Internal notes for my own file, not a client email?
faq.a: That's Transcript to Meeting Notes. A lapsed client with no transcript is Client Follow-up.

faq.q: Is it safe to paste client details?
faq.a: Paste only what the deliverable needs. Nothing you paste is stored by the skill, but the chat itself is a record — treat it like any other working document.

faq.q: It did something odd. Who do I ask?
faq.a: Brandon Mason. Say which skill and what you said to start it; a screenshot of the reply helps.
